The second coming of Christ (the central figure) at the end of time, surrounded by saints and angels with the final judgment of the living and the dead. The fresco includes over 300 figures. 22ND NOVEMBER 2026 ~ OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST , KING OF THE UNIVERSE Christmas Cards are for sale in the Parish Office - €7.00 for a pack of six cards SOLEMNITY OF CHRIST THE KING On the last Sunday of each liturgical year, the Church celebrates Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe, or Christ the King. This solemnity reminds us that while governments come and go, Christ reigns as King forever. Pope Pius XI instituted this feast in 192 5 for the Roman Rite of the Catholic Church. Originally, it was celebrated on the last Sunday in October but in 1970, it was moved to the last Sunday in Ordinary Time and thus to the end of the li turgical year. Christ’s kingship is rooted in the Church’s teaching on the Incarnation. Jesus is fully God and fully man. He is both the divine Lord and the man who suffered and died on the Cross. One person of the Trinity unites himself to human nature and reigns over all creation as the Incarnate Son of God. The Solemnity today reminds us of a King who is present in the least of a ll: The King identifies himself directly with the hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked, sick, and imprison ed. Serving or neglecting people in need counts as serving or neglecting Christ himself. Today’s Gospel, Matthew 25:31-46, challenges us all to follow the exam ple of Jesus, the King of the universe, who is present in the less fortunate of our society.
